→
\(\href{symbols/binders.html}{\rightarrow}\)
 Logical Connective (Primitive) Fm × Fm → Fm | Bool × Bool → Bool | Type × Type → Type [Primitive / Undefinable] Natural-Language Definition: Material implication (“if 𝛂 then 𝛃”) asserting that truth of the antecedent 𝛂 entails truth of the consequent 𝛃; in Variant 2 (MKTD2), the non-dependent function type constructor A → B ≡ Π(_:A), B. Characterized axiomatically by A01 (Weakening), A02 (Frege's distribution), and Rule 1.14 (Modus Ponens). (Personal Page →) 1.01 (A01 Weakening) · 1.02 (A02 Frege) · 1.14 (Modus Ponens)
⟷
\(\href{symbols/prop-bool.html}{\longleftrightarrow}\)
 Logical Connective (Defined / Axiomatic) Fm × Fm → Fm | Bool × Bool → Bool [Defined] Formal & Natural-Language Definition: Logical bi-implication (equivalence, “𝛂 if and only if 𝛃”), formally defined as mutual implication: (𝛂 ⟷ 𝛃) ≡ ((𝛂 → 𝛃) ∧ (𝛃 → 𝛂)). (Personal Page →) 1.03–1.05 (∧ Rules) · 3.01 (Extensionality ⟷)
∧
\(\href{symbols/prop-bool.html}{\land}\)

Characterized by A03 (left projection), A04 (right projection), and A05 (pairing introduction). (Personal Page →) 1.03 (A03 ∧-Elim 1) · 1.04 (A04 ∧-Elim 2) · 1.05 (A05 ∧-Intro)
∨
\(\href{symbols/prop-bool.html}{\lor}\)

Characterized by A06 (left injection), A07 (right injection), and A08 (case analysis). (Personal Page →) 1.06 (A06 ∨-Intro 1) · 1.07 (A07 ∨-Intro 2) · 1.08 (A08 ∨-Elim)

\(\href{symbols/prop-bool.html}{\neg}\)

(Personal Page →) 1.09 (A09) · 1.10 (A10) · 1.12 (A12 LEM)

∈
\(\href{symbols/typing-colon.html}{\in}\)
 Binary Predicate Symbol (Kernel Primitive) Class × Class → Bool | Class.Expression × Class.Expression → Fm [Primitive / Undefinable] Natural-Language Definition: The fundamental undefinable binary relation of class theory, read “class x is a member (element) of class Y”. Because it is the primitive membership relation at the root of the ontology, it is not defined in terms of prior notions; instead, it is governed by Class Comprehension (3.01 / 4.06), Sethood (3.02: x set ⟷ ∃(Y:Class)(x ∈ Y), i.e., only sets can be members of classes), and Extensionality (3.09). Never used for typing (use :). (Personal Page →) 3.01 (Comprehension Rule) · 3.02 (Sethood Def) · 3.09 (Extensionality) · 4.06 (Comprehension Schema)
=

A × A → Bool [Primitive / Axiomatic] Natural-Language & Axiomatic Definition: Identity / equality of objects of the same type (“X and Y denote the exact same mathematical entity”). On classes, characterized by Left/Right Soundness of Membership (3.07–3.08: equal classes have the same elements and belong to the same classes), Class Extensionality (3.09: (∀(z:Class)((z∈X)⟷(z∈Y))) → (X=Y)), and Intensionality (3.10). (Personal Page →) 3.07 (Left ∈-Soundness) · 3.08 (Right ∈-Soundness) · 3.09 (Extensionality) · 3.10 (Intensionality)

 Kernel Quotation & Antiquotation Operators (Primitive) A → A.Expression | A.Expression → A [Primitive / Undefinable Reflection Operators] Natural-Language Definition: Explicit syntax quotation ‹e› suspends evaluation of an expression e:A and returns its syntactic AST object of type A.Expression (e.g., ‹𝛗› : Fm = Bool.Expression). Antiquotation / evaluation ⟦u⟧ splices or evaluates a syntactic expression u:A.Expression back into semantic level A. Binder-variable splice ⦃v⦄ injects a metavariable v:Variable into a binding site. (Personal Page →) 3.21 (Quotation in Class Conditional) · 4.01 (Meta-Instantiation) · 4.06 (Comprehension Schema) · 5.01 (Löb's Theorem)

\(\href{symbols/enc.html}{\mathsf{Enc} / \mathsf{Dec} / \mathsf{Emb} / \mu_A / \mathsf{eval}}\)
 Kernel Reflection & Coding Symbols (Primitive) A.Expression → Class | Type.Expression → Type [Primitive / Undefinable Metatheoretic Operators] Natural-Language Definition: Enc is the injective Gödel-Dunaev coding mapping syntactic AST objects into first-order classes; Dec is its partial inverse decoding class codes back into syntax; Emb embeds lower-level objects into higher sorts; μ_A / eval interprets syntactic expressions into their semantic denotation in model/conglomerate A. (Personal Page →) 3.21 (Enc in FV guard) · 3.71 (Soundness of 𝘛) · 4.01 (eval(A).Expression) · 4.02 (Generalisation)
FV / Ctx.FV / FFI / NFV
\(\href{symbols/hygiene-ffi-fv.html}{\mathsf{FV} / \mathsf{Ctx.FV} / \mathsf{FFI} / \mathsf{NFV}}\)
 Kernel Syntactic Hygiene Symbols (Primitive) A.Expression → Class | A.Expression × Variable × Fm → Bool [Primitive Syntactic Hygiene Operators] Natural-Language Definition: FV(e:A.Expression) returns the class of encoded free variables occurring unbound in syntactic expression e (strictly requiring .Expression sort such as Fm or Class.Expression, never semantic Bool). FFI((t:X.Expression),x,(𝛗:Fm)) holds iff no free variable of t becomes captured when substituted for free occurrences of x in 𝛗. NFV(X,x,(𝛃:Fm)) asserts that x:X does not occur free in 𝛃:Fm.
